note: CP-1 revision dialogue trees. A speaker (one NPC) uses a tree by its group; the game fills the {variables} from real state (purse, hold, prices, the recruit's own record). Node fields: text | texts [{if, text}] | pages [text...] (Enter continues), set [flags], options [{label, next | action, arg, if [flags], enable_if [flags], hint}]. Flags are computed by port_game.gd (has_fish, never_fished, poor, crew, afford, met, hired, rich, full_crew...), '!flag' negates. Actions: leave, trade, hire, track (arg: a target id), pay (arg: reales, next on success, fail on too poor), map. Every speaker is a man; the Canon content rules apply to every line.

options.label: Hire {rname}   ({cost} reales, you are {missing} short)
options.hint: You are {missing} reales short. Fish, sell, come back.

options.label: What would you do aboard my ship?
How do I earn the coin?

skills.text: {effect}  He asks {cost} reales once, and your purse holds {reales}.

earn.text: Fish pays. Sail to a ground, lower the nets, come home and sell at the Fish Market. The nearest ground is {nearest_ground}.

options.label: Mark the fishing ground on my map
Mark the Fish Market on my map

tracked.text: {track_name} is marked: {track_dist}. Open the map (M) or follow the arrow at the top of the screen.

texts.text: Barnaby Gull, fishmonger of Fish Row. I buy by the kilo and I weigh honest. That is {hold_kg} kg you carry, Captain: about {hold_value} reales on my board today.
Barnaby Gull, fishmonger of Fish Row. I buy by the kilo and I weigh honest. Nothing in your hold, Captain: sail out, cast your nets, come back with something that still smells of the sea.

options.label: Sell my catch   (the hold is empty)
options.hint: The hold is empty. Fish first.

options.label: Where do I find the fish?
Why does the price drop when I sell a lot?

where.text: Four grounds worth the sail: Pilchard Shallows, close and kind; Gannet Bank, richer and farther; Kelp Reef, for the patient; Blue Drop, where the yellowfin run, and you want a hand aboard for that water.

options.label: Mark the nearest ground on my map

depth.text: A market is a conversation, Captain. Sell me forty kilos of one fish and I stop listening. The price climbs back in about six days; sell me a little of everything and I never stop smiling.

texts.text: {greeting} Good catch you've got there. Keep it out of the sun.
{greeting} That sloop of yours wants nets, Captain. The sea is generous to anyone who shows up.

fishing.text: Mackerel thick at Gannet Bank this morning; sardines everywhere in the Shallows. Under one knot and a quiet sea, the nets work. Go faster and they only drag.

grounds.text: Pilchard Shallows south-west, an easy sail. Gannet Bank south-east, follow the birds. Kelp Reef and Blue Drop are far; you will want a hand or two.

options.label: Mark Pilchard Shallows on my map
Mark Gannet Bank on my map

tracked.text: {track_name}: {track_dist}. Look for the buoys and the circling gulls.

when.text: Dawn and dusk, friend. Fish bite when the light is thin. Night is for sleeping, or for the brave: fewer fish, and the dark sits heavy.

tip.text: Take the north edge of the Kelp Reef at dusk, and let nobody see you do it. The big snappers lie under the weed. (A true tip, and now you owe me a story.)

broke.text: Three reales, Captain. You have {reales}. Pay me when you can afford my silence.

texts.text: {greeting} Fish in your hold? The fishmonger under the red canopy buys by the kilo.

options.label: What sells well in this port?

tracked.text: {track_name}: {track_dist}. Mind the bridge over the Cut.

gossip.text: Yellowfin pays three times what sardines do, but the Blue Drop is a long sail and the fish will not wait for you. Sell a mix, keep the price alive. That is all a merchant knows.

broke.text: Five reales for the truth, Captain. You carry {reales}. Fish first, pay later.

texts.text: {greeting} Hired a hand already? Good: a ship with one pair of arms waits for help.

options.label: What is moving on the quay?
Is there work for a captain?
Where do I find hands for my ship?

cargo.text: Salt fish out, rope and tar in, and whatever the customs clerk lets through. Barrels up, crates down. That is the whole of life on the wharf.

work.text: Not until you have a crew and a hold. Right now the best work for a sloop is fishing: it is honest and the market takes all you bring. Cargo contracts come later.

tracked.text: {track_name}: {track_dist}. Ask him politely; hands are proud this season.

texts.text: {greeting} Short of coin? Everyone starts that way. Fish, sell, hire. That is the harbour's whole advice.

options.label: What is the sea like out there?

sea.text: South of the cove the water is kind. Past Gannet Bank the swell lengthens and the wind pulls harder. Mind the green zone on your compass: sail into the wind and the ship stops dead.

wares.text: {wares} (The chandlers' counters open to captains with a crew and a route: that comes in a later module. For now, look all you like. Looking is free.)

business.text: The harbour is busy and the street is loud, so yes. Fish Row feeds half the city, the quay feeds the other half, and the Hill pays for the rest.

texts.text: {greeting} If you are looking for work, Captain, the notice board by the pier lists those who need a berth.

tracked.text: {track_name}: {track_dist}. Follow the main streets; the city is bigger than it looks from the sea.

lore.text: Anvil Harbor has stood on this shore for two hundred years. The Quay below, the markets in the middle, the Hill above, where the Governor's household keeps the view. The tide takes some, the walls keep the rest.

safe.text: Safe enough while the lamps are lit and the bells are honest. Keep your hands on your own purse and out of anyone else's, and we will get on.

governor.text: The Governor keeps the Palace on the Hill. He does not receive captains without a letter and a ship worth the berth. Come back with a crew and a name.

tracked.text: {track_name}: {track_dist}. Up the Palace Road and the long stair. No running on the stair.

options.label: May I ask about the Hill?
Is there profit in this harbour?

hill.text: The Hill is where the city keeps its dignity: the Palace, the long gardens, a view of every mast that comes home. We prefer our captains to arrive by the front stair.

profit.text: There is profit in everything that floats, Captain, but it is made in the warehouses and the Customs House, not on the quay. Keep your books clean and your ship cleaner.

options.label: A mug and the rumours   (2 reales)
Looking for hands for my ship.

broke.text: Two reales for a mug, Captain. You have {reales}. The soup is free if you do the washing.

crowd.text: Sailors with a week's pay, dockers with a day's, merchants who never pay, and the odd captain who is none of the above. The Rusty Anchor feeds them all.

tracked.text: {track_name}: {track_dist}. Tell him the Anchor sent you; he will give you a better price. He will not.

options.label: How do I register a ship?

dues.text: None for a fishing sloop under the Harbour Charter. Cargo is another matter: that ledger opens later in your story, Captain.

register.text: Your sloop is already on the harbour roll: berth at the pier, no charge. The Customs House keeps the roll, in a very large book, in a very quiet room.

tracked.text: {track_name}: {track_dist}. The building with the clock tower.
